clauses.scope_note: MPL-2.0 §4; distribution of Covered Software where statute, judicial order, or regulation makes compliance with some or all license terms impossible.
clauses.condition_explanation: The predicate requires compliance with all license terms that remain possible despite the legal impediment.

obligation_items.content: Comply with the License to the maximum extent possible.
obligation_items.object: Covered Software affected by the legal impediment
obligation_items.trigger: When compliance with any License term for some or all Covered Software is impossible due to statute, judicial order, or regulation.

clauses.scope_note: MPL-2.0 §4; applies to all distributions of the affected Covered Software under the License when legal impossibility prevents compliance with any term.
clauses.condition_explanation: The limitations description must identify the limitations and affected code, be included in a text file with all such distributions, and, except where prohibited by statute or regulation, be sufficiently detailed for a recipient of ordinary skill to understand.

obligation_items.content: Describe the limitations and the code they affect in a text file included with every distribution of the affected Covered Software under the License; except to the extent prohibited by statute or regulation, provide enough detail for a recipient of ordinary skill to understand.
obligation_items.object: Text file accompanying each distribution of the affected Covered Software
obligation_items.trigger: When compliance with any License term for some or all Covered Software is impossible due to statute, judicial order, or regulation; the detail requirement is subject to the stated legal-prohibition exception.

clauses.scope_note: MPL-2.0 §5.1; rights granted by a particular Contributor terminate automatically on failure to comply with any License term. This captures the resulting restriction on exercising those rights, subject to the stated reinstatement provisions.
clauses.condition_explanation: Grants are provisionally reinstated upon becoming compliant unless the Contributor explicitly and finally terminates them. They become ongoing if the Contributor fails to notify You of non-compliance by reasonable means before 60 days after compliance. They also become ongoing if the Contributor gives reasonable notice, it is the first notice of non-compliance from that Contributor, and You comply before 30 days after receiving it.

obligation_items.content: Do not exercise rights granted by a Contributor while those rights are terminated and have not been reinstated under §5.1.
obligation_items.object: Covered Software rights granted by the noncompliance-affected Contributor
obligation_items.trigger: After failure to comply with any License term, while the relevant Contributor's rights remain terminated and before any applicable reinstatement; reinstatement is subject to the express notice, cure-period, and final-termination terms.

clauses.scope_note: MPL-2.0 §5.2; termination affects grants from all Contributors for the Covered Software under §2.1. Excludes declaratory-judgment actions, counterclaims, and cross-claims.
clauses.condition_explanation: The trigger is You initiating litigation against any entity by asserting a patent-infringement claim alleging that a Contributor Version directly or indirectly infringes a patent; the listed excluded actions do not trigger termination.

obligation_items.content: Do not exercise §2.1 rights granted by any Contributor for the Covered Software after those grants terminate under §5.2.
obligation_items.object: Covered Software rights granted by any Contributor under §2.1
obligation_items.trigger: When You initiate qualifying patent-infringement litigation as described in §5.2.

clauses.scope_note: MPL-2.0 §5.3; end-user license agreements validly granted by You or Your distributors before termination survive termination. Distributors and resellers are excluded from this survival rule.
clauses.condition_explanation: The agreement must have been validly granted under the License before termination under §5.1 or §5.2, and must be an end-user agreement rather than one for a distributor or reseller.

clauses.scope_note: MPL-2.0 §10.2; Covered Software may be distributed under the version under which You originally received it or a subsequent version published by the license steward.
clauses.condition_explanation: The license-version choices are alternatives, not cumulative requirements. This is permission, not an obligation to adopt a later version.

clauses.scope_note: MPL-2.0 §10.3; applies to creating a new license for software not governed by the MPL, not to relicensing Covered Software under a renamed MPL.
clauses.condition_explanation: If You create software not governed by the License and want to create a new license for it, You may create and use a modified version of this License only if it is renamed and references to the license steward are removed, except to note that the modified license differs from this License.

obligation_items.content: Rename the modified license and remove references to the license steward, except a reference identifying that the modified license differs from this License.
obligation_items.object: Modified version of the MPL used as a new license for software not governed by the MPL
obligation_items.trigger: When You create and use a modified version of this License to license software not governed by the MPL.

clauses.scope_note: MPL-2.0 §10.4; applies to distribution of Source Code Form that is Incompatible With Secondary Licenses under this version of the License.
clauses.condition_explanation: The Exhibit B notice must be attached when both the stated incompatibility and distribution under this License version apply.

obligation_items.content: Attach the notice described in Exhibit B to the Source Code Form.
obligation_items.object: Source Code Form that is Incompatible With Secondary Licenses
obligation_items.trigger: When You choose to distribute that Source Code Form under this version of the License.

clauses.scope_note: MPL-2.0 Exhibit A; permits an alternative location for the Exhibit A notice when placing it in a particular file is not possible or desirable.
clauses.condition_explanation: The alternative may be a location such as a LICENSE file in a relevant directory where a recipient would be likely to look for the notice.

clauses.scope_note: MPL-2.0 Exhibit A; permits adding additional notices of copyright ownership.
clauses.condition_explanation: Any additional copyright-ownership notices must be accurate.

Sections 5.1–5.3 establish automatic termination, conditional reinstatement, patent-litigation termination, and survival of specified prior end-user licenses.
Warranty disclaimer and assumption-of-risk terms do not create an activity constraint for this extraction.

Court, venue, and governing-law provision; excluded legal venue material.
